proof_decision.trust_question: Do the Planning ownership repairs preserve truthful stacked-lane state, do unsynchronized source runtimes fail with executable recovery, and are semantic task routes and explicit inventory patches authority-neutral and isolated from ambient worktree state?
proof_decision.narrowest_evidence: The existing focused Planning scenarios pass, including atomic lane creation/binding, explicit-lane new-plan reciprocal parent binding, supersede input ownership, current-work preservation, and lane-activation recovery. Hosted package proof exposed that the reciprocal assertions were attached to the adjacent activation scenario; they now reside in the existing explicit-lane new-plan owner and both exact scenarios pass. All 34 existing source-checkout launcher scenarios pass with missing-dependency proof folded into the two-checkout runtime-identity scenario. Nine existing semantic-route owner scenarios pass. The single #2941 inventory fixture proves isolated baseline-plus-patch validation, ambient-state exclusion, patch-owned invalid-file and deletion handling, clean-worktree equivalence, and unchanged full-tree staged-deletion refusal. Ruff and generated command-package static/native Node proof pass.
proof_decision.prune_or_replacement_condition: Keep assertions in their existing owner tests and retain the combined launcher and inventory scenarios while they remain the narrowest faithful boundaries. Consolidate consumer-only route assertions when one typed conformance matrix can preserve source revision, staleness, and non-authority; do not add separate suites for already-covered runtime or inventory paths.
proof_decision.residual_risk: Hosted CI remains the cross-platform proof for generated adapters and Git/tar behavior. The explicit patch audit is intentionally broad over its isolated subject and took longer than the 30-second shell yield; unrelated broad pytest suites were omitted under the repository test strategy.
